newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht rockets offshore, speculators squeezed.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht rockets offshore, speculators squeezed.

text.p: The Thai baht rocketed to a 13-year-high in offshore markets on Thursday as speculators scrambled to scoop up baht while selling dollars heavily to cover short positions.
Thailand's central bank added fuel to the fire by denying market talk that it might buy dollars at 24.00 baht to help ease the woes of offshore speculators caught short of baht.
"We have no interest whatsoever to buy dollars in the offshore market," a senior central bank official told Reuters.

The baht on Thursday morning rallied to 23.800/24.000 offshore from 24.360/24.410 late on Wednesday, its highest level against the dollar since the baht was devalued in 1984. The central bank fixed the midrate at 25.82 to the dollar.
The spread between the offshore and onshore market rates widened sharply. In the local market, the baht was quoted much weaker, at around 25.855 to the dollar.
Dealers said the demand for baht was heightened as long dollar/baht outright positions of one-month duration were due to mature next week.

Some offshore funds were reluctant to roll over the majority of their long dollar/baht positions in the forward market as the central bank showed no signs of soon ending an informal two-tier market system it created last month after a speculative attack on the Thai unit.

The central bank last month blocked baht supplies to foreign speculators who attacked the currency, thinking it would be devalued. That forced the speculators to pay exorbitant rates to acquire baht elsewhere and resulted in what offshore dealers called a "bloodbath."

"This morning, reportedly, U.S. lifers (life insurance firms) were looking to unwind long dollar/baht worth US$300-500 million. But the current liquidity conditions simply do not permit," said a report from Singapore-based research house I.D.E.A.
"The result -- dollar/baht nose-dived (to a) 13-year low...Critically, it seems like these funds are far too long dollar/baht," the report said.
The heavy demand drove baht/dollar one-month swap premiums up to 130/170 satangs per dollar offshore compared with 20/30 satangs in the domestic market.
Dealers said there was talk that the central bank would likely keep the two-tier market intact for another four to eight weeks to monitor the situation and punish speculators.
"If that is the case, we could see the baht surge as high as 23.00 baht to the dollar soon," said a dealer at one foreign bank here.

I.D.E.A said in a report that offshore currency markets expected the Thai central bank to keep the three-week-old measure to curb market attacks on the baht until domestic economic indicators show more positive signs.
